clue.text: Substitute train for strap hangers only?

parts.note: a substitute is a stand-in
to train a horse or a protege is to groom it

explanation.surface: A commuter grumbles that the replacement train left the passengers hanging on straps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substitute train' reads as a replacement service, but the two words are separate pieces, the noun STAND-IN and the verb GROOM. Strap hangers are standing passengers holding the straps.
explanation.definitionFit: Space where passengers can only stand, holding the straps, is the kind of accommodation meant.

clue.text: To produce notes about a bad actor can be humiliating

indicators.note: about means the singing word goes around the actor word

parts.note: producing musical notes with the voice is singing
a ham is an overacting, poor performer

explanation.surface: A poor performer bursting into song brings embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting someone to shame is humiliating them.

clue.text: A superior assistant

parts.note: superior means better

explanation.surface: A helper who outranks the others.
explanation.definitionFit: An abettor or abetter is someone who helps, often in wrongdoing, so an assistant.

clue.text: Wanted to show the Camp town knight can

annotationWithheld.why: Wanted to show the Camp town knight can: SIR (knight) + ABLE (can) is clear, but no reading of 'the Camp town' gives DE, so the clue as held looks garbled by OCR
annotationWithheld.clue: Wanted to show the Camp town knight can

clue.text: A little Parisienne at home in a Welsh town

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman from Paris has settled comfortably in a small Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: NEATH is a town in South Wales; the definition includes 'in', since the Parisienne is at home in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Neath is a market town in South Wales, near Swansea.

clue.text: Say repeatedly others were given food

parts.note: the rest are the others
those who were given food ate

explanation.surface: Someone keeps saying that the others have already been fed.
explanation.definitionFit: To restate is to say something again.

clue.text: The guy getting into oil's possibly Turkish

indicators.note: getting into puts the man inside the rearranged oil letters
possibly says the letters of the word oil's may be arranged another way

parts.note: the possessive s counts as a letter here
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: A man moving into the oil business might be Turkish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The guy' looks like the subject of the sentence but simply gives the man. Osmanli is an old word for Ottoman, from the dynasty's founder Osman.
explanation.definitionFit: Osmanli is an old name for an Ottoman, a Turk of the old empire, and so also means Turkish.

clue.text: Bows — such nonsense!

definitions.meaning: the bows used to play violins, a fiddle's sticks
an old-fashioned exclamation dismissing something as rubbish

explanation.definitionFit: A fiddler's bows are the sticks of the fiddle, and the word is also an exclamation like 'rubbish!'.

clue.text: One calls -safety first! when confused

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
to call someone something is to name them

indicators.note: first says to take only the opening letter of the word safety

explanation.surface: An alarmed person shouts for safety first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something muddled or disordered is in a mess.

clue.text: Thought like a pressman after all

indicators.note: after puts the pressman piece behind the all piece

parts.note: as means like
the sum is the whole, all of it
ED, short for editor, is a newspaper man

explanation.surface: Just what you would expect of a journalist, after all.
explanation.definitionFit: Assumed means supposed or taken for granted, the same as thought in that sense.

clue.text: Deeming Rates in need of reform, but conflict

indicators.note: something that needs reform must be reshaped, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Thinking local taxes need overhauling leads to a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates were the old British local property tax, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A disagreement is a clash of views, a conflict.

clue.text: Shiftless fellow giving a leftist backing about break

indicators.note: about puts the turned leftist word around the break word
backing means the leftist word is written backwards

parts.note: a red is a communist or left-winger
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: An idle man supports a left-winger over some quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shiftless' means lazy and lacking initiative, not literally without shifts; 'giving' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A drifter is an aimless person with no settled job, shiftless in the sense of lacking drive.

clue.text: Wild animals savaging a hen say

indicators.note: savaging tears the words apart, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Beasts attacking a chicken, so to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyaenas, an older spelling of hyenas, are wild carnivores of Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Forever acquiring silver, being keen

indicators.note: acquiring means the forever word takes the silver inside it

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, forever
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Always eager to get hold of more silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Being eager means being enthusiastic, keen.

clue.text: On the side of the German in flat accommodation

indicators.note: in places the German article within the flat word

parts.note: flat means dull, boring
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A German lodging in a flat, next door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodation' completes the picture of the German being housed in the flat; 'flat' means dull here, not an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: To border on something is to lie along its edge, alongside it.

clue.text: Turned up one's nose?

parts.note: the phrase usually means showing disdain, but here describes a nose that points upward at the tip

explanation.definitionFit: Retroussé, from French, describes a nose turned up at the tip.

clue.text: A confused statement will result

indicators.note: confused says the letters of the word statement are mixed up

explanation.surface: A muddled declaration will be the outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will' looks like part of the verb 'will result' but is the noun, a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will is a legal document disposing of property after death, called a testament.

clue.text: Looked on William as flighty creature

parts.note: to look on is to watch, so saw
Bill is a short form of William

explanation.surface: Watching William, one sees a fickle sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A sawbill is a duck with a serrated beak, such as a merganser, a bird that flies.

clue.text: Decline a prize

parts.note: a trophy is a prize such as a cup

explanation.surface: Turn down an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' reads as refuse, but it means waste away.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrophy is wasting away or declining, of a muscle or an institution.

clue.text: Let the trainee rest

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a trainee driver's car
ease means rest, relaxation

explanation.surface: Allow the apprentice to have a break.
explanation.definitionFit: To lease property is to let it out for rent.

clue.text: Going after an old palace

parts.note: something going after another comes later

explanation.surface: Pursuing an ancient royal residence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lateran in Rome was the papal palace for centuries.

clue.text: Inoffensive, lacking aspiration, so short of members

indicators.note: aspiration is the breathed h sound, so the letter H is dropped

parts.note: harmless means inoffensive

explanation.surface: Someone mild and unambitious, without any limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Members are limbs, so without arms is missing some members.

clue.text: People listed in Yellow Pages?

parts.note: the business directory is reread as pages listing people who are yellow, meaning lacking courage

explanation.definitionFit: Yellow means cowardly, so a list of yellow people would be of the faint-hearted.

clue.text: Copper surrounded by children move quickly!

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the copper inside the children word

parts.note: seed is offspring, children in the biblical sense
a penny, P, is a copper coin

explanation.surface: A police officer, ringed by kids, is told to hurry up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer, but it is a penny, P.
explanation.definitionFit: To speed is to go fast, to hurry.

clue.text: Work it back without saying a word that's much the best

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: back says the word it is written in the reverse direction

parts.note: keeping mum means staying silent

explanation.surface: Doing the job quietly and in reverse turns out best.
explanation.definitionFit: The optimum is the most favourable or best possible.

clue.text: Steps outside very quietly in a dotty way

indicators.note: outside puts the steps word around the musical marking

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps over a fence
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quietly

explanation.surface: Someone tiptoes softly outside, behaving a bit oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dotty' means crazy on the surface but literally made of dots: to stipple is to paint in dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Stipple work is painting or engraving in small dots.

clue.text: A patient stitcher

parts.note: patient reads as an adjective, a tolerant sewer, but is the noun: one who stitches up those in hospital

explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon stitches up the wounds of those under treatment.

clue.text: Engaged in sport as planned, yet is in poor shape

indicators.note: something in poor shape needs remaking, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Took part in a game as arranged, though out of condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in poor shape' rearranges PLANNED YET into PLAYEDTENN, and IS is kept as written at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing a match with rackets on a court is a sport one engages in.
